ei.subject: 수능특강Light 영어
ei.title: It was early October, and the weather couldn't have been better for hiking.

fullPassage: It was early October, and the weather couldn't have been better for hiking. Ryan slowly followed the mountain path, listening to the soft sounds of the forest around him. The afternoon sunlight felt warm on his skin, and he paused now and then, enjoying the quiet peace of being alone. Leaves moved lightly in the gentle wind, and he felt pleased far away from his usual worries. Then, he heard a strange sound behind him. He turned quickly and looked around. He didn't see anything, but he was certain he had heard something. And it wasn't the blowing of the wind or the falling of a twig. Someone — or something — was moving nearby. A sudden chill went through him, and his heart began beating fast.

questions.passage: It was early October, and the weather couldn't have been better for hiking. Ryan slowly followed the mountain path, listening to the (A)[harsh / soft] sounds of the forest around him. The afternoon sunlight felt (B)[warm / cold] on his skin, and he paused now and then, enjoying the quiet peace of being alone. Leaves moved lightly in the (C)[gentle / violent] wind, and he felt pleased far away from his usual worries. Then, he heard a strange sound behind him. He turned quickly and looked around. He didn't see anything, but he was certain he had heard something. And it wasn't the blowing of the wind or the falling of a twig. Someone — or something — was moving nearby. A sudden chill went through him, and his heart began beating fast.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 부드러운(soft), 따뜻한(warm), 부드러운(gentle).
det.analysis:
✅ ① soft — warm — gentle: 숲의 '부드러운' 소리, '따뜻한' 햇살, '부드러운' 바람 — 평화로운 하이킹 묘사에 적합.
❌ ② harsh — warm — gentle: harsh(거친)는 평화로운 숲과 반대.
❌ ③ soft — cold — gentle: cold(차가운)는 10월 따뜻한 햇살과 반대.
❌ ④ soft — warm — violent: violent(난폭한)는 부드러운 바람과 반대.
det.tip: soft ↔ harsh, warm ↔ cold, gentle ↔ violent

questions.passage: It was early October, and the weather couldn't have been better for hiking. Ryan slowly followed the mountain path, listening to the soft sounds of the forest around him. The afternoon sunlight felt warm on his skin, and he (A)[paused / rushed] now and then, enjoying the quiet peace of being alone. Leaves moved lightly in the gentle wind, and he felt (B)[annoyed / pleased] far away from his usual worries. Then, he heard a (C)[familiar / strange] sound behind him. He turned quickly and looked around. He didn't see anything, but he was certain he had heard something. And it wasn't the blowing of the wind or the falling of a twig. Someone — or something — was moving nearby. A sudden chill went through him, and his heart began beating fast.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 멈추다(paused), 기쁜(pleased), 이상한(strange).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ paused — pleased — strange: 이따금 '멈추며' 고요를 즐기고, 걱정 없어 '기뻤고', '이상한' 소리를 들었다는 문맥에 적합.
❌ ① rushed — pleased — strange: rushed(서둘렀다)는 평화롭게 즐기는 상황과 반대.
❌ ② paused — annoyed — strange: annoyed(짜증난)는 pleased와 반대.
❌ ④ paused — pleased — familiar: familiar(익숙한)는 후속 공포 반응과 모순.
det.tip: pause ↔ rush, pleased ↔ annoyed, strange ↔ familiar

questions.passage: It was early October, and the weather couldn't have been better for hiking. Ryan slowly followed the mountain path, listening to the soft sounds of the forest around him. He didn't see anything, but he was (A)[doubtful / certain] he had heard something. And it wasn't the blowing of the wind or the falling of a twig. Someone — or something — was moving (B)[nearby / far away]. A (C)[gradual / sudden] chill went through him, and his heart began beating fast.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 확신하는(certain), 가까이(nearby), 갑작스러운(sudden).
det.analysis:
✅ ② certain — nearby — sudden: 들었다고 '확신하고', 무언가가 '가까이' 움직이고 있었으며, '갑작스러운' 오싹함이 훑고 지나갔다는 문맥에 적합.
❌ ① doubtful — nearby — sudden: doubtful(의심스러운)은 '확신'과 반대.
❌ ③ certain — far away — sudden: far away는 nearby와 반대 — 가까이 움직여야 긴장감.
❌ ④ certain — nearby — gradual: gradual(점진적인)은 '갑작스러운 오싹함'과 반대.
det.tip: certain ↔ doubtful, nearby ↔ far away, sudden ↔ gradual

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ loud(시끄러운) → gentle(부드러운). 평화로운 10월 하이킹 상황에서 바람은 '부드러운' 것이 자연스러움.
det.analysis:
✅ ① soft: 부드러운 → 적절
✅ ② warm: 따뜻한 → 적절
✅ ③ alone: 혼자인 → 적절
❌ ④ loud → gentle: 원문은 gentle wind. 평화로운 분위기에 loud는 반대.
det.tip: gentle wind = 부드러운 바람 ↔ loud wind(시끄러운 바람)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ doubtful(의심하는) → certain(확신하는). '듣지는 못했지만 뭔가 들었다고 확신했다'는 원문.
det.analysis:
✅ ① pleased: 기쁜 → 적절
✅ ② strange: 이상한 → 적절
✅ ③ twig: 잔가지 → 적절
❌ ④ doubtful → certain: he was certain(그는 확신했다)이 원문. doubtful은 반대.
det.tip: certain ↔ uncertain. be certain = 확신하다

det.korean: ③ warmth(온기) → chill(오싹함, 한기). 공포 상황에서 '갑작스러운 오싹함'이 훑고 지나갔다는 원문.
det.analysis:
✅ ① turned: 돌았다 → 적절
✅ ② nearby: 가까이 → 적절
❌ ③ warmth → chill: sudden chill(갑작스러운 한기)이 원문. warmth(온기)는 공포 상황과 반대.
✅ ④ fast: 빠르게 → 적절 (심장이 빠르게 뛰다)
det.tip: chill(오싹함/한기) ↔ warmth(온기). 공포의 신체 반응

❌ ① jumped: 뛰었다 — 평화로운 하이킹과 맞지 않음
❌ ③ shouted: 소리쳤다 — 고요와 반대
❌ ④ fell: 넘어졌다 — 문맥 무관

det.tip: now and then = from time to time = occasionally = at times

det.korean: gentle = 부드러운, 온화한. harsh = 거친.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ harsh: 거친 — gentle의 반의어.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 sudden과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: sudden = 갑작스러운. gradual = 점진적인.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ gradual: 점진적인 — sudden의 반의어.
❌ ① abrupt: 갑작스러운 — sudden과 유사

questions.passage:
(A) The afternoon sunlight felt warm on his skin, and he paused now and then, enjoying the quiet peace of being alone.

(B) The word <u>pause</u> can also mean something quite different in another context.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 paused/pause의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) (동사) 잠시 멈추다 (B) (명사) 멈춤, 중단.
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 잠시 멈추다(동사) — (B) 멈춤(명사): (A)에서 paused는 '멈추었다'(동사 과거), (B)에서 pause는 '멈춤/중단'(명사).
❌ ② (A) 명사 — (B) 동사: 반대 배치
❌ ③ (A) 중단하다 — (B) 쉬는 시간: 부분 맞으나 형태 설명 불명확
❌ ④ (A) 시작하다 — (B) 속도: 둘 다 틀림
det.tip: pause: 동사(잠시 멈추다) / 명사(멈춤). 동일 형태 동·명사 다의어

❌ ① slow: 느린 — 반대
❌ ② planned: 계획된 — 반대
❌ ④ gradual: 점진적인 — 반대
det.tip: sudden = abrupt = unexpected

det.korean: listening. 분사구문(동시동작)으로 주어 Ryan이 들으면서 따라간 능동 상태이므로 현재분사 listening.
det.analysis: listen → listening. 분사구문: 주어가 '듣는' 능동 동시동작 → 현재분사.
det.tip: 분사구문 현재분사 = 능동 동시동작. while listening

questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.analysis: beat → beating. begin + V-ing (동명사) 또는 begin + to-V. 원문은 beating.
det.tip: begin + V-ing / begin + to-V 모두 가능. 여기선 beating.
